name: EPHB4-related Capillary Malformation-Arteriovenous Malformation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for CM-AVM2

criteria.description: Presence of multiple small, round to oval capillary malformations with pale halos
Identification of fast-flow arteriovenous malformations or fistulas by imaging
Detection of pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in the EPHB4 gene
Family history of similar vascular anomalies consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic capillary malformations and arteriovenous malformations combined with a pathogenic EPHB4 mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential to confirm diagnosis and differentiate from CM-AVM1 caused by RASA1 mutations.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Multiple small round to oval capillary malformations with pale halos
searchTerms: multiple small red skin spots with pale rings
tiny round capillary marks with halos
small vascular skin lesions with light edges

pathognomonic.symptomName: Recurrent spontaneous bleeding from arteriovenous malformations

common.symptomName: Localized soft tissue swelling overlying vascular malformations
searchTerms: localized swelling over blood vessel malformations
soft tissue lump above vascular lesion

common.symptomName: Warmth and pulsatility over arteriovenous malformations
searchTerms: warm, pulsing area over vascular malformations
feeling of heat and pulse in AVM area
small red spider veins near capillary spots
tiny dilated blood vessels near lesions
mild asymmetry of arms or legs

occasional.symptomName: Neurological symptoms secondary to intracranial arteriovenous malformations
searchTerms: nerve problems due to intracranial vascular malformations

occasional.symptomName: Skin ulceration overlying large arteriovenous malformations
searchTerms: skin sores over large vascular malformations
open wounds on vascular lesion areas

occasional.symptomName: High-output cardiac failure in extensive arteriovenous malformations
searchTerms: high-output cardiac failure due to vascular malformations

rare.symptomName: Seizures due to cerebral arteriovenous malformations
Hemorrhagic stroke from ruptured intracranial arteriovenous malformations
searchTerms: hemorrhagic stroke due to ruptured vascular malformations
brain bleed caused by AVM rupture

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; coagulation studies may be required if bleeding occurs
imaging: Doppler ultrasound showing fast-flow vascular malformations
MRI/MRA demonstrating arteriovenous malformations and fistulas
Conventional angiography for detailed vascular mapping
other: Histopathology of capillary malformations showing dilated capillaries with thin walls

distinguishingFeatures: RASA1 gene mutations instead of EPHB4
Similar capillary malformations but may have different vascular lesion distribution
Family history and genetic testing differentiate
Presence of mucocutaneous telangiectasia and recurrent epistaxis
Pulmonary and cerebral arteriovenous malformations more common

redFlags: Rapid enlargement or bleeding of vascular malformations
Neurological deficits or seizures indicating intracranial involvement
references: Eerola I, Boon LM, Mulliken JB, et al. Capillary malformation-arteriovenous malformation, a new clinical and genetic disorder caused by RASA1 mutations. Am J Hum Genet. 2003.
Amyere M, Boon LM, Vikkula M. EPHB4 mutations cause a second form of capillary malformation-arteriovenous malformation (CM-AVM2). Hum Mol Genet. 2017.
